canonical_answers: Solving RC dV/dt+V=0 gives V=V₀e^{-t/RC} and I=-(V₀/R)e^{-t/RC}.

payload.text: A capacitor C initially at voltage V₀ discharges through resistance R at t=0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: A valid design varies the resistance R as the independent variable, measures the resulting time constant τ (from the slope of ln V vs. t) as the dependent variable, and holds the capacitance C and initial voltage V₀ constant as controls, consistent with V=V₀e^{-t/RC}.
required_evidence: dependent variable: measured time constant τ=RC
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show independent variable: resistance R; dependent variable: measured time constant τ=RC; control: constant C and V₀.

parts.prompt: State the governing principle (Kirchhoff's voltage law) and the initial-condition assumption V(0)=V₀ for an ideal RC loop, and explain why each must hold for the measurement to isolate the time constant.
